title: Silicon Deficiency in Plants: Signs, Causes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: Silicon Deficiency in Plants: Signs and Fixes
metaDescription: Silicon deficiency shows on the young leaves first. See the signs crop by crop, what causes it, and the fertilizer sold here that fixes it.
excerpt: Silicon deficiency in plants starts on the young leaves and the growing tip. Silicon is not one of the nutrients every plant must have. But rice and sugarcane take up more of it than of any other mineral. They lay it down in the walls of their leaves and stems, which keeps them stiff and upright, harder for insects to chew and for blast and brown spot to enter. Better at holding water in a dry spell. Here are the signs in each crop, what brings it, how to be sure and the fertilizer that fixes it.

blocks.text: Once silicon is laid down in a leaf it stays there, so the plant cannot move it to new growth. The signs show on the whole plant: soft, drooping leaves, weak stems and more disease than in the fields around.
Silicon deficiency symptoms

Rice leaves feel soft and droop instead of standing up, so the canopy opens and the lower leaves sit in shade. Brown spot, blast and stem borer do more harm, stems lodge, and more grains stay empty. Sugarcane shows tiny pale freckles on the older leaves that face the sun, thinner stalks and weaker ratoons.

blocks.text: What causes silicon deficiency

Old, deeply weathered and leached soils hold little silicon, and so do peat and sandy soils. Every crop carries silicon away in its straw or cane. So fields cropped two or three times a year with the straw burned or hauled off run down fastest. Heavy nitrogen makes the leaves softer and the shortage worse.
How to be sure it is silicon

Lodging also follows too much nitrogen, strong wind and stem borers, and brown spot also goes with potassium shortage. In sugarcane, eyespot and rust spots have a ring or an orange powder, while silicon freckles have neither. In rice the surest check is a straw test: straw at harvest with less than 5 percent silicon is short. In sugarcane, a leaf test of the top visible dewlap leaf with less than about 1 percent silicon is low. A soil test for available silicon, and a test strip given silicate beside the rest of the field, confirm it.
How to fix silicon deficiency

Put the straw back into the field and spread rice hull ash or burnt rice hull. On sugarcane mill mud and boiler ash. For a faster fix, mix 1 to 2 tons of a calcium silicate or silicate slag per hectare into the soil at land preparation, or 1 to 3 tons for sugarcane. It also lowers soil acidity a little, the way lime does.
A potassium silicate spray at the label rate, at tillering and again at booting in rice, gives the leaves a quick lift. But the soil dose lasts longer.

How to keep silicon deficiency away
Return the straw or the cane trash to every crop instead of burning it, add rice hull ash, compost and mill mud. Split the nitrogen so the leaves never grow too soft.

blocks.title: Too much is a problem too
blocks.text: Silicon does no harm in the amounts a farmer applies. But silicate slags differ in what else they carry, so buy a registered product and follow its label.

blocks.text: Silicon deficiency questions

items.q: Is silicon a nutrient for rice?
items.a: It is not one of the nutrients every plant must have, but rice takes up a great deal of it. Enough silicon keeps the leaves upright and the stems strong, and it cuts blast, brown spot and lodging.

items.q: What is the best source of silicon for rice?
items.a: The straw of the last crop plowed back in, and rice hull ash, cost the least. Calcium silicate or a registered silicate fertilizer works faster where a soil or straw test reads low.

items.q: Does burning rice straw cause silicon deficiency?
items.a: Burning leaves much of the silicon in the ash. But the ash is easily blown or washed away, and straw carried off the field takes all of its silicon with it. Over many seasons the soil runs down.
